events.subtitle: Dizzy Gillespie Birthday

venue.name: Dizzy's Club at Jazz at Lincoln Center

events.factual_description: Jazz at Lincoln Center presents Dizzy Gillespie Birthday with Jon Faddis at Dizzy's Club on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, with sets at 19:00 and 21:00. JALC identifies Faddis as a protégé and longtime standard-bearer of Gillespie's legacy and says the quartet will explore Gillespie favorites including A Night in Tunisia, Groovin' High, and Manteca. The announced quartet is Jon Faddis on trumpet, David Hazeltine on piano, Todd Coolman on bass, and Dion Parson on drums. The current ticket page lists a standard $60 face-value cover plus a $5 fee and a $25 student face-value reservation charge plus a $5 fee; student reservations require valid student ID. Dizzy's Club also requires a $25 minimum food and/or beverage purchase per person.

en.why_it_matters: Faddis carries Gillespie's language from direct contact rather than repertory study alone, and this quartet puts that lineage back on the horn through tunes like A Night in Tunisia, Groovin' High, and Manteca. The useful reason to notice the date is the continuity: a protégé returning to the vocabulary, humor, high-register attack, swing, and Afro-Cuban spark that Gillespie helped make modern.
en.trip_verdict: If New York is already in play and October 21 fits cleanly, this is a worthwhile Dizzy's set to catch. I would not build a dedicated DMV-to-NYC trip around the date by itself.

es.why_it_matters: Faddis carga el lenguaje de Gillespie desde el contacto directo, no sólo desde el repertorio, y este cuarteto vuelve a poner ese linaje en la trompeta con piezas como A Night in Tunisia, Groovin' High y Manteca. La razón concreta para mirar la fecha es la continuidad: un discípulo regresando al vocabulario, el humor, el ataque en el registro alto, el swing y la chispa afrocubana que Gillespie ayudó a volver modernos.
es.trip_verdict: Si Nueva York ya está en juego y el 21 de octubre embona limpio, vale entrarle a uno de los sets en Dizzy's. No armaría un viaje dedicado DMV–NYC sólo alrededor de esta fecha.

events.subtitle: A Tribute to Art Blakey's Jazz Messengers

venue.name: Dizzy's Club at Jazz at Lincoln Center

events.factual_description: Jazz at Lincoln Center presents Carl Allen's Messengers of Jazz — A Tribute to Art Blakey's Jazz Messengers at Dizzy's Club from October 22 through October 25, 2026. Thursday through Saturday have 19:00 and 21:00 sets; Sunday has 17:00 and 19:30 sets. JALC says Art Blakey once named Carl Allen an honorary Messenger and frames the sextet around musicians associated with the Jazz Messengers, with repertoire including Moanin' and Blues March. The announced lineup is Brian Lynch, Donald Harrison, Robin Eubanks, Benny Green, Alexander Claffy, and Carl Allen. The current ticket page lists a standard $55 face-value cover plus a $5 fee and a $25 student face-value reservation charge plus a $5 fee; student reservations require valid student ID. Dizzy's Club also requires a $25 minimum food and/or beverage purchase per person.

en.why_it_matters: The tribute has unusually concentrated lineage. Allen was personally recognized by Blakey as an honorary Messenger, while Lynch, Harrison, Eubanks and Green each bring their own lived relationship to the Messengers tradition. Putting that history into a sextet with Allen driving from the drum chair makes Moanin' and Blues March less a repertory exercise than a conversation among musicians who inherited the language through people, bands and bandstands.
en.trip_verdict: If a New York trip overlaps October 22–25, actively make room for one set. Four nights give enough flexibility that the engagement should fit around the trip rather than dictate the trip by itself.

es.why_it_matters: El tributo concentra el linaje de una manera poco común. Blakey reconoció personalmente a Allen como Messenger honorario, mientras Lynch, Harrison, Eubanks y Green cargan sus propias relaciones vividas con la tradición de los Jazz Messengers. Poner esa historia en un sexteto con Allen empujando desde la batería hace que Moanin' y Blues March funcionen menos como ejercicio de repertorio y más como conversación entre músicos que heredaron el lenguaje a través de personas, bandas y escenarios.
es.trip_verdict: Si un viaje a Nueva York coincide con el 22–25 de octubre, sí le haría espacio activamente a uno de los sets. Cuatro noches dan suficiente flexibilidad para acomodarlo dentro del viaje en vez de dejar que la fecha dicte el viaje completo.

events.subtitle: The Pulse of Miles Davis

venue.name: Dizzy's Club at Jazz at Lincoln Center

events.factual_description: Jazz at Lincoln Center presents Greg Hutchinson's Kind of Now: The Pulse of Miles Davis at Dizzy's Club from Wednesday, October 28 through Saturday, October 31, 2026, with 19:00 and 21:00 performances. JALC describes the project as a drummer-led tribute to the drummers who powered Miles Davis's ensembles, using Davis's musical legacy as a platform for groove, improvisation and forward-looking reinterpretation. The announced quintet is Marquis Hill on trumpet, Antoine Roney on tenor saxophone, Gerald Clayton on piano, Robert Hurst on bass, and Greg Hutchinson on drums. The current ticket page lists a standard $65 face-value cover plus a $5 fee and a $25 student face-value reservation charge plus a $5 fee; student reservations require valid student ID. Dizzy's Club also requires a $25 minimum food and/or beverage purchase per person.

en.why_it_matters: The concept puts the rhythm section where it belongs in the Miles story: at the engine room. Hutchinson is not simply leading another Davis tribute; the project listens through the drummers who changed the feel underneath Miles, then hands that rhythmic question to a quintet with Hill, Roney, Clayton and Hurst. That makes the repertoire a vehicle for pulse, space and improvisational response rather than a museum set of familiar tunes.
en.trip_verdict: If New York is in play during October 28–31, actively make room for one set. Four nights give enough flexibility to fit the project around the trip rather than making the engagement the sole reason to travel.

es.why_it_matters: El concepto pone a la sección rítmica donde debe estar en la historia de Miles: en el cuarto de máquinas. Hutchinson no está encabezando simplemente otro tributo a Davis; el proyecto escucha a través de los bateristas que cambiaron el pulso debajo de Miles y entrega esa pregunta rítmica a un quinteto con Hill, Roney, Clayton y Hurst. Así, el repertorio funciona como vehículo para pulso, espacio y respuesta improvisada, no como museo de temas conocidos.
es.trip_verdict: Si Nueva York está en juego entre el 28 y el 31 de octubre, sí le haría espacio activamente a uno de los sets. Cuatro noches dan suficiente flexibilidad para acomodarlo alrededor del viaje en vez de volver la residencia la única razón para desplazarse.
